questions.q: What does S3 actually store, and how is it accessed?
options: Objects (files plus metadata and a unique key) inside buckets, accessed via an HTTP(S) API
Raw disk blocks, mounted directly as a local filesystem on an EC2 instance
Only database table rows, accessed via SQL
Files that must always be attached to exactly one EC2 instance
questions.explain: S3 is object storage — key-addressed objects in buckets, reached over an API, not mounted like a disk.

questions.q: Why do S3 storage classes like Standard, Standard-IA, and Glacier exist?
options: To trade retrieval speed for price, letting infrequently accessed or archival data cost much less to store
To limit which AWS Region a bucket can be created in
To control which IAM users are allowed to access a bucket
To determine how many Availability Zones a bucket can span
questions.explain: Storage classes are a cost/retrieval-speed tradeoff — the data itself is the same, just stored and priced differently.

questions.q: What is EBS, and how does it differ from S3?
options: EBS is block storage — a virtual disk attached to exactly one EC2 instance — while S3 is object storage not attached to any instance
EBS and S3 are two names for the exact same underlying service
EBS is used only for storing website images, never for databases
EBS has no size limit while S3 volumes are capped at 100 GB
questions.explain: EBS provides a mountable, per-instance virtual disk; S3 provides API-accessed object storage decoupled from any single instance.

questions.q: Why is S3, not EBS, the default choice for a data pipeline's raw and staged files?
options: S3 isn't tied to any single instance, so any compute (Glue, Lambda, Athena, Redshift) can read and write it directly over the API
EBS cannot store more than one file at a time
S3 is always faster to read from than EBS for every workload
EBS charges a per-object retrieval fee that S3 does not
questions.explain: S3's decoupling from any specific compute instance is exactly why it works as shared storage across a pipeline's different services.

questions.q: What is a typical use case for EBS within a data pipeline architecture?
options: Providing the root or data volume for an EC2 instance, such as one running a database engine
Serving as the primary landing zone for raw pipeline files read by Athena
Acting as the object storage backend queried directly by Redshift Spectrum
Replacing S3 entirely as the pipeline's shared data store
questions.explain: EBS shows up underneath compute that needs a real, mounted disk — not as the shared data layer S3 provides.
